evidence:
host/store-node-host.lisp:1512-1513
  (equal (len (fn-sf-successes after-files))
         (1+ (len (fn-sf-successes before-files))))
books/store-files.lisp:117 fn-sf-successes is `(fn-sl-list (fn-sf-successes-field s))`. For the snoc form, fn-sl-list is fn-sl-rev-take, which builds a fresh reversed list (books/snoc-list.lisp:62-66). fn-sl-count (snoc-list.lisp:116) gives the count in O(1).
fix: Compare `(fn-sl-count (fn-sf-successes-field ...))` of after and before instead.
reviewer: host/store-node-host.lisp:1512-1513 compares (len (fn-sf-successes ...)) before and after. fn-sf-successes (books/store-files.lisp:117) is fn-sl-list, which for the snoc form calls fn-sl-rev-take and builds a fresh O(N) list (books/snoc-list.lisp:62-66), while fn-sl-count (snoc-list.lisp:116-120) is O(1). The function is reached through fnn-bridge-finish, the default *fnn-finish-callback* (io.lisp:1809, 1816), and through fn-xw-finish (store-write-host.lisp:1390). The cost is two O(N) allocations per standalone commit, which contradicts the comment at 1497-1503. The composed owner binds its own callback, and the offline `store post` already pays O(N) to replay at open, so the impact is small.
scenario: Each standalone finish (the default *fnn-finish-callback*, host/native/io.lisp:1809/1816, used by the offline `store post`; store-write-host's fn-xw-finish calls it too) allocates two O(N) copies of every success acknowledgement in the store's history, only to compare their lengths. The comment directly above (1497-1503) claims the finish no longer walks the history.
title: fn-store-sn-finish copies the whole successes history twice per commit to compare lengths
